entries.text: ClickHouse Local (chDB) now runs the full TPC-H and TPC-DS specification: concurrent throughput streams, TPC-H refresh functions RF1 and RF2, and TPC-DS data maintenance. Every stream opens its own chDB session on the same database path, so in-memory databases are refused.
details: chDB has no transactions, so refresh and maintenance steps run without BEGIN or COMMIT and cannot be rolled back; a failed step needs a reload.
chDB reports no deleted-row count, so RF2 counts the matching keys once before the RF2 timer starts; the RF2 time covers the deletes only.
The three TPC-DS returns deletes run as an uncorrelated tuple IN subquery because chDB rejects a correlated EXISTS in a delete.

entries.text: Result bundles record transactional on every TPC-H refresh function and TPC-DS maintenance operation, so a reader can tell refresh steps that ran without a transaction from steps that ran inside one. Bundles written earlier load as transactional.
CedarDB now runs TPC-DS data maintenance, so a full-specification TPC-DS run (load, power, throughput, maintenance) works on CedarDB.
CedarDB result bundles now record the server release (for example v2026-09-29) as the platform version instead of unknown.
TPC-H refresh functions now use the schema's lower-case key column names, so they work on case-sensitive engines such as ClickHouse.
